messages:
maria: Pushed a new synthetic fixture generator for promptsets (branch eval/synth-fixtures). CI started failing nondeterministically for a few eval jobs, looks like sample counts / ids differ between shards. Anyone seen this?
lee: I saw 3 failed shards on CI with hash mismatches: `fixtures_v2.tar.gz` vs `expected.tar.gz`. Quick logs: `ERROR: fixture manifest mismatch (count 500 != 500)` but different ids.
sanjay: probable cause: RNG seed not wired. generate_fixtures defaults to system time if --seed not provided. That will make different shards and cause metric variance.
maria: repro locally with these steps:
```
PYTHONPATH=. pytest tests/eval/runner_test.py::test_fixture_consistency -k fast
python tools/generate_fixtures.py --promptset chatbot --n 500 --seed=42 --out fixtures_v2.tar.gz
```
If I omit `--seed` the file changes every run.
lee: CI calls the tool without seed currently (legacy behavior). So shard A/B/C produce different sets -> aggregations and cached eval artifacts diverge.
olivia: eval-bot: [alert] quantized-run-7 produced -1.3% BLEU vs baseline on fixture set 'chatbot_small' (p=0.02). Might be noise from different fixtures.
maria: Plan suggestion: 1) Enforce `--seed` in generator or derive seed deterministically from git commit. 2) Add CI verification: fail if generator ran without explicit seed. 3) Store fixture artifact checksum in the eval job manifest and compare on shard startup.
sanjay: Also: write the seed and git commit into the fixture `manifest.json` during generation, e.g. `{\"seed\": 42, \"git_commit\": \"abc123\"}` so downstream can repro exactly.
lee: I'll open a small CI patch to run `tools/verify_fixtures.py --artifact $ARTIFACT` as part of shard setup and fail early.
maria: Quick patch idea for deterministic default if no seed passed: use commit hash -> seed int:
```
import hashlib
commit = os.getenv('GIT_COMMIT') or subprocess.check_output(['git','rev-parse','HEAD']).strip().decode()
seed = int(hashlib.sha1(commit.encode()).hexdigest()[:8], 16) % (2**31)
```
That keeps runs reproducible per commit.
lee: Nice. Also add an assertion in tests: `assert len(set(ids)) == len(ids), \"duplicate ids in fixtures\"` to catch accidental duplicates.
olivia: Can we also run an overlap/leakage quick-check against training corpora? Even small overlaps can bias evals. A lightweight bloom/hash check would be fine.
sanjay: agree. Suggest `tools/check_overlap.py --fixtures fixtures_v2.tar.gz --corpora data/train/* --threshold 0.001` and fail if above threshold.
maria: Good call. We'll add an explicit `overlap_pct` field to the manifest and publish it with artifact metadata.
lee: For CI artifact retention: some of these fixture artifacts get GC'd quickly and cause flakiness when comparing to older baselines. We should bump retention for fixture artifacts to 30 days.
ops-bot: @maria noted. Created ticket INFRA-432 to increase artifact retention to 30 days :calendar:
maria: I'll open PRs: 1) generator -> require/derive seed + write manifest + overlap check, 2) verify_fixtures CI step, 3) small test assertions, 4) dashboard panel for fixture stability. Target: PRs within next 2 hours.
olivia: +1 to dashboard: panels: fixture-stability, seed-diff (counts of differing ids between runs), overlap-percentage, nightly-regression alerts.
sanjay: also add a tiny nightly smoke job that runs generate_fixtures + small eval (10 prompts) to catch quantization/runner regressions fast.
maria: sounds good. tagging @ops and @platform for artifact retention and CI lanes. I'll include the dashboard JSON and a minimal `verify_fixtures.py` in the PR.
lee: LGTM. If anyone wants to pair on the CI change ping me.
maria: thanks all — going to draft PRs now.
